_comment: The 11 canonical PDLC stages. design-system.md §8.1: these are canonical and drive StageRail. The 7-chip lifecycle row on the landing screen is an orientation summary only, derived from lifecycleGroup below, and is not interactive. The pilot's 5-chip rail is retired.

stages.name: Idea Vetting
stages.purpose: Establish whether an idea is worth pursuing and capture it as a vetted artifact.

stages.name: JPD Idea / HLIS
stages.purpose: Register the idea for discovery and size it at high level.

stages.name: Prioritization
stages.purpose: Rank the idea against the portfolio.

stages.name: Requirement Lock
stages.purpose: Fix the scope and the acceptance criteria.

stages.name: Solution Lock
stages.purpose: Agree the high-level design and the non-functional envelope.

stages.name: User Experience
stages.purpose: Design the interaction and the visual system.

stages.name: LLD & Stories
stages.purpose: Elaborate the design to implementation detail and decompose into stories.

stages.name: Development
stages.purpose: Implement the stories and review the changes.

stages.name: Testing
stages.purpose: Assess testability and execute the test strategy.

stages.name: Deployment
stages.purpose: Release the change through change management. Never performed by an agent (DEC-28).

stages.name: Release & Run Support
stages.purpose: Operate, monitor and report on the released change.

_emptyStageNote: A stage with no agents renders as 'Available in a later release' and is not selectable (screen-specs §1.4.3). The PoC enables 4 of 11 stages; the rail still shows all 11 because stage completion is a property of the epic (FR-NAV-009).
